description: In chain_walk, the per-cert policy check at line 1947 (policy-f: explicit_policy==0 && tree==None) fires BEFORE the §6.1.5(a) leaf counter decrement (lines 1973-1985). For the leaf cert (i==0), this means the counter is not yet decremented when the per-loop check fires. The final check at line 2415 (after the loop) re-checks the same condition and is the authoritative leaf check. However, the in-loop check at line 1947 runs BEFORE §6.1.5(a-b) finalisation, meaning for a leaf cert where explicit_policy becomes 0 only after §6.1.5(b) forces it to 0, the per-loop check would not catch it. Conversely, if explicit_policy is decremented in §6.1.5(a) and becomes 0, the in-loop check fires AFTER §6.1.5(a) (which is inside the i==0 block which runs BEFORE the end-of-loop state update). Verify: trace through RFC 5280 §6.1 algorithm ordering for the leaf step — §6.1.3(d)(e)(f) are per-cert, §6.1.5 is post-loop finalization. The in-loop policy-f check at line 1947 correctly fires after §6.1.3(d) but §6.1.5(a-b) should not run inside the loop at all — it should only run after the loop ends.
notes: Revised priority: functionally correct due to dual check (in-loop at line 1947 + post-loop at 2415). The structural placement of §6.1.5(a-b) inside the for-loop at i==0 gives identical semantics to post-loop execution because i==0 is always the last iteration. No observable correctness difference exists. The concern is code clarity: the comment says §6.1.5(a-b) which is a post-loop RFC section, but it runs inside the loop. Could confuse future maintainers matching code to RFC structure.
title: policy-f check fires before §6.1.5(a) leaf counter decrement
